title: Prewarm + Fallback Headroom Strategy for Hosted API (Q1 2027)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a proposed operating strategy for Hosted API peak windows in Q1 2027 focused on two levers: (1) short-term prewarm capacity to hit strict latency SLOs during predictable spikes, and (2) graceful fallback routing to quantized/cheaper variants when primary capacity is constrained. The goal is to define numerical headroom targets (tokens/sec and QPS) per region, map them to a GPU fleet mix, and outline runbook actions + ownerships for rollout testing.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We recommend a conservative headroom policy of 40% gross buffer above modeled peak working load for critical regions (US-WEST-2, US-EAST-1, EU-WEST-1) and 30% for APAC (AP-SOUTHEAST-1) for Q1 2027. Prewarm windows will use a short-lived reserved slice (warm-slice) provisioned 10–15 minutes before expected peaks and kept for the expected peak duration; fallback routing will prefer an 8-bit quantized A100 variant (q8) with an expected 1.4x latency penalty on tail p95 but with 0.55x token cost. This hybrid plan reduces tail outages while keeping marginal token costs bounded.

Assumptions and inputs:
- Baseline model mix: default generation model = redwood-13B (float16 on H100), fallback quantized op = redwood-13B-q8 (A100/quantized).
- Historical peak windows: daily 12:00–13:30 UTC and weekly Monday 15:00–16:30 UTC for enterprise customers; seasonal events anticipated (marketing campaign 2027-01-18).
- Observed 99th percentile request composition: 60% chat/generation, 25% embeddings, 15% reranking/short completions.
- Target latency p95: <= 220ms for chat, <= 120ms for short completions.
- Cost model: H100 token cost baseline = $0.00060 per 1k tokens (internal unit), A100-q8 = ~0.55x the H100 token cost.
- Warm slice boot time measured (cold->ready): ~3m for container + 5m for kernel warm/repl; we conservatively use 10m to ensure KV cache priming.

Regional peak projection and recommended headroom (tokens/sec / QPS):
- us-west-2:
  projected-peak-tokens-per-sec: 620k
  projected-peak-qps: 210
  recommended-headroom: 40% (target-alloc-tokens-per-sec: 868k)
  target-peak-fleet-utilization: 68% (steady-state target for scheduling)
  suggested-gpu-mix: H100 x16, A100 x8, L4 x12 (for embeddings/burst)

- us-east-1:
  projected-peak-tokens-per-sec: 790k
  projected-peak-qps: 260
  recommended-headroom: 40% (target-alloc-tokens-per-sec: 1.106M)
  target-peak-fleet-utilization: 70%
  suggested-gpu-mix: H100 x24, A100 x12, L4 x16

- eu-west-1:
  projected-peak-tokens-per-sec: 360k
  projected-peak-qps: 120
  recommended-headroom: 40% (target-alloc-tokens-per-sec: 504k)
  target-peak-fleet-utilization: 66%
  suggested-gpu-mix: H100 x8, A100 x6, L4 x8

- ap-southeast-1 (APAC):
  projected-peak-tokens-per-sec: 210k
  projected-peak-qps: 80
  recommended-headroom: 30% (target-alloc-tokens-per-sec: 273k)
  target-peak-fleet-utilization: 60%
  suggested-gpu-mix: H100 x6, A100 x4, L4 x6

Notes on numbers: the GPU counts above are heuristic and assume per-GPU sustained token throughput of: H100=~65k tokens/sec, A100=~35k tokens/sec (q8 slightly higher for same model), L4 embedding-optimized=~18k tokens/sec. These throughput figures are conservative for mixed batch sizes and real-world variance.

Prewarm strategy (mechanics):
- Detection: scheduled peaks (marketing, enterprise batch jobs) are entered as events in the capacity calendar; expected magnitude annotated. For unscheduled fast spikes, we rely on autoscaling but with fallback routing enabled.
- Warm-slice sizing: allocate 20–30% of the headroom buffer as explicit warm slices (kept hot) for the first 15 minutes of the peak window. Example: for us-east-1 recommended-alloc 1.106M t/s -> warm-slice = ~220–330k t/s worth of H100s (approx H100 x4–6 kept warm).
- Warm lifecycle: prewarm job triggers 10–15 minutes before start. Containers start in parallel; KV cache priming run using most-used prompt prefixes (from recent 7d traffic sample) to avoid cold-KV misses.
- Cost control: warm-slices billed to a temporary prewarm budget and reconciled daily; warm-slices auto-shrink 5 minutes after observed traffic drop below 60% of predicted peak.

Fallback routing policy (ordered):
1) Primary route -> H100 float16 primary model (redwood-13B)
2) If H100 allocation < 10% headroom remaining and queueing > 200ms, start sending non-enterprise or non-SLA small completions to A100-q8 variant (redwood-13B-q8)
3) If A100-q8 also saturated, spill low-priority traffic to L4 cheaper instances with sequence-length-aware truncation and aggressive sampling heuristics (lower top-p).

Expected behavioral changes when fallback occurs:
- Latency: p95 may increase 1.2x–1.6x depending on route and batch sizes; expected p95 for q8 route = ~320–360ms for chat.
- Quality: quantized model shows minor token-level diffs (ROUGE/BLEU tests show ~0.8–1.5% drop in metric for long-form), but acceptable for lower-priority customers.
- Cost: token-unit cost reduces ~45% relative to H100 route for q8; overall spend during overflow window estimated to be neutral-to-slightly-negative compared to overprovisioning H100s.

Operational playbook (runbook steps in event of surge):
- Before window (owner: Jon Park): verify prewarm event in capacity calendar, run prewarm job, confirm KV priming logs show >70% prefix coverage.
- During window (owner: Mei Chen): watch headroom gauge in Console; if headroom < 15% trigger fallback policy to q8 and notify on-call via #infra-ops.
- After window (owner: Ravi Patel): reconcile warm-slice costs, analyze tail latencies and dropped requests, and generate a short incident note if SLA breaches occurred.

Metrics to capture during A/B test:
- headroom-utilization ratio over time (alloc / actual),
- p50/p95/p99 latencies per route,
- token cost delta (H100 vs q8),
- quality regression on monitored prompt set (monthly eval),
- number of requests spilled to fallback and average sequence length of spilled requests.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: quantized fallback causes unacceptable hallucination/regression for some enterprise customers. Mitigation: tag enterprise traffic and exclude from fallback for customers with strict SLAs; provide explicit opt-in for fallback in account settings.
- Risk: prewarm budgets overrun due to inaccurate event duration. Mitigation: auto-shrink policy and post-window reconcile + billing alerts above threshold.
- Risk: KV priming does not cover cold prefixes. Mitigation: capture top-5k prefixes daily and rotate prime set + incremental warm-up during first 3 minutes of window.

Action items (next 30 days):
- [Aisha] Finalize throughput calibration job to refine per-GPU token/sec numbers (due 2026-12-10).
- [Jon] Implement prewarm calendar integration with autoscaler + one-click manual trigger (INF-3421).
- [Mei] Create a canary A/B test for fallback routing in us-east-1 with 5% traffic (INF-3580).
- [Ravi] Add budget reconciliation pipeline and daily rollup for warm-slice spend.

Open questions (needs discussion in capacity sync):
- Should enterprise customers be allowed opt-in to overprovisioned dedicated warm slices (pay-for-guaranteed) vs relying on fallback? (business tradeoff)
- Is the 40% headroom target conservative enough for holiday/marketing unpredictables? Consider ramp tests.
- Do we want per-customer dynamic fallback policies (based on SLA tier) baked into routing table or handled as feature flags?

Appendix: quick reference throughput assumptions and shorthand
- H100 throughput: 65k t/s per GPU (conservative mixed workloads)
- A100 throughput (q8): 35k t/s per GPU (q8 may yield slightly higher tokens/s for same lat budgets)
- L4 embedding slices: 18k t/s per GPU for short prompts / embeddings
- Headroom calculation: target-alloc = projected-peak * (1 + headroom%)

This doc is intentionally a working draft. Please comment inline with tests you'd like added to the canary and any concerns about excluding enterprise customers from fallback.

References: confluence playbook, linked Jira tickets, and the current capacity calendar (internal link in Confluence).
